guard: the completion check runs ahead of EVERY verdict, not only ahead of the red one
completionMarker: an absolute --config path is read where it is

mutations.name: the completion check is disabled outright
mutations.expectRed: a run that never reaches the suite's end is INCONCLUSIVE, not KILLED
mutations.note: Disabling the check outright is BROADER than the cell it would like to name: in a fail-fast suite the earlier incomplete-run cell fires first, so this is graded on that one and the clean-exit direction is graded by the ordering mutation below, which is the narrow one.

mutations.name: THE ORDERING: the completion check applies only to a red run, as it did before
mutations.expectRed: a CLEAN exit that never reached the region is INCONCLUSIVE, not SURVIVED

mutations.name: a run that printed nothing is blamed on the assertion instead
mutations.expectRed: a run with NO OUTPUT is named as never having started

mutations.name: an exit code alone is enough for a PASS again
mutations.expectRed: a suite whose teardown forces exit 0 over real failures is not a SURVIVED

mutations.name: the failure vocabulary is widened until it fires on a clean run
mutations.expectRed: ...while a change nothing tests is still SURVIVED on that same suite
mutations.note: A pattern matching the word 'failed' anywhere fires on the summary line of a CLEAN run ('0 failed'), which turns every genuine survivor into a WRONG-RED. Narrowness is the whole design of this default.

mutations.name: the word boundary after FAIL is relaxed away
mutations.expectRed: the word boundary after FAIL is load-bearing: a cell LABEL containing `FAILING` is not a failure
mutations.cell: the word boundary after FAIL is load-bearing: a cell LABEL containing `FAILING` is not a failure
mutations.note: A real near-miss from a neighbouring lane, not an invented string: a passing cell whose LABEL says FAILING would become evidence that the suite failed, which turns a genuine SURVIVED into a WRONG-RED and hides the finding a kill set exists to produce.
mutations.completionMarker: an absolute --config path is read where it is

mutations.name: FAILED is matched case-insensitively
mutations.expectRed: ...while a change nothing tests is still SURVIVED on that same suite
mutations.cell: ...while a change nothing tests is still SURVIVED on that same suite
mutations.note: The other measured near-miss. Prose about a failed REPLY is ordinary suite vocabulary; the verdict word is the shouted one. RE-AIMED after the first run graded it WRONG-RED at 20 marks. Broader than the cell it named: the fixture's own output carries lowercase `failed` prose, so a case-insensitive vocabulary reddens the SURVIVED cell at mark 20 before the boundary cell at mark 25 is ever reached, and this file stops at its first red. That is the STRONGER proof, not a weaker one -- the harm is demonstrated on a real run rather than on a string this file typed for itself -- and the boundary cell stays as the statement of WHICH boundary carried it.
mutations.completionMarker: an absolute --config path is read where it is

mutations.name: the non-zero anchor on the failure count is dropped
mutations.expectRed: ...while a change nothing tests is still SURVIVED on that same suite
mutations.cell: ...while a change nothing tests is still SURVIVED on that same suite
mutations.note: `0 failed` is what every clean run of a counting suite prints, so without the anchor the grader reads a green summary as a failure and no counting suite can ever report SURVIVED. RE-AIMED after the first run graded it WRONG-RED at 20 marks, and for the same reason: `0 failed` is what the fixture's own clean run prints, so dropping the anchor reddens the SURVIVED cell first. A mutation must be no broader than the cell it names, and in a fail-fast file `no broader` is decided by ordering, not by intent.

mutations.name: the vocabulary is WIDENED by a word these four strings do not contain
mutations.expectRed: ...and it is EXACTLY the measured pattern, so a relaxation these strings miss still fails here
mutations.cell: ...and it is EXACTLY the measured pattern, so a relaxation these strings miss still fails here
mutations.note: The reason the literal is pinned at all. This change is invisible to every behaviour cell above -- none of the four strings contains PANIC -- and it is still a guessed convention entering a grader that is only allowed to carry a measured one. Without the pin it survives.
